mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen in each of the last three weekly means (-22.4 to -18.9 to -17.4 to -13.3), and this own-series recovery momentum persists because trip habits formed during the climb carry forward, so the next 28-day mean exceeds the trailing 28-day mean.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC rose from -22.4 at t-3w to -13.3 at t-0w, a 9.1 point gain
failure_condition: The mean of RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is less than or equal to the mean over the trailing 28 days, so the four-week change is non-positive.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT has recovered 10.5 points in three weeks (-37.1 to -26.6); once the weekly TRANSIT mean crosses above -28, station throughput is high enough to sustain non-essential trip chains, which lifts RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT weekly mean crosses above -28 percent from baseline (t-0w -26.6 is the first crossing)
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved -37.1, -32.9, -30.4, -26.6 across the four weekly means
failure_condition: In the two weeks after TRANSIT first exceeds -28, the following 14-day mean of RETAIL_REC is not higher than the prior 14-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL's steady decline (9.0 to 5.1) shows households leaving home more each week; combined with the PARKS rise (-14.4 to 5.6), this out-of-home substitution generates discretionary trips that raise RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell 9.0 to 5.1 while PARKS rose -14.4 to 5.6 over the same four weeks
failure_condition: In weeks where RESIDENTIAL declines and PARKS rises jointly, the next 14-day mean of RETAIL_REC is not above its trailing 14-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: The PARKS series has swung 20 points in three weeks (-14.4 to 5.6), the signature of a seasonal outdoor shift; warm-weather outdoor leisure substitutes for paid indoor retail-and-recreation venues, so RETAIL_REC's forward four-week mean stays below its trailing mean.
candidate_trigger: PARKS weekly mean exceeds +5.0 percent from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS went from -14.4 at t-3w to +5.6 at t-0w, crossing zero at t-2w
regime_hint: spring seasonal transition into outdoor weather
failure_condition: While PARKS weekly means remain above +5.0, the next-28-day mean of RETAIL_REC exceeds its trailing-28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL falls monotonically (9.0, 7.3, 6.3, 5.1), so time-at-home is shrinking week over week; once RESIDENTIAL drops below +5.5, displaced home time converts into retail trips and the same-week RETAIL_REC mean rises.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL weekly mean falls below +5.5 percent from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined in every week, 9.0 then 7.3 then 6.3 then 5.1
failure_condition: In the week after RESIDENTIAL first prints below +5.5, the weekly RETAIL_REC mean is not higher than the prior week's mean.

mechanism_narrative: Continued WORKPLACES recovery (-17.0 to -11.3) pulls daytime hours and commuting back into offices; that time reallocation reduces weekday leisure capacity, so once WORKPLACES crosses above -12 the forward four-week RETAIL_REC mean is lower than the trailing mean.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES weekly mean rises above -12.0 percent from baseline (t-0w -11.3 is the first crossing)
failure_condition: Over the four weeks after WORKPLACES first exceeds -12, the mean of RETAIL_REC is at or above its trailing-28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Residual stay-at-home policy is still visible in RESIDENTIAL holding 5.1 points above baseline; while that gap persists, out-of-home discretionary capacity is capped and RETAIL_REC's forward two-week mean does not exceed its trailing mean.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL weekly mean remains above +5.0 percent from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL stayed positive all four weeks (9.0, 7.3, 6.3, 5.1) while WORKPLACES stayed below -11
regime_hint: residual stay-at-home policy regime with partial reopening
failure_condition: While RESIDENTIAL stays above +5.0, the next-14-day mean of RETAIL_REC is higher than its trailing 14-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has plateaued near +9 (8.7, 9.0, 9.3, 9.1), showing essential-trip demand is saturated; with TRANSIT also recovering, incremental trips shift to discretionary categories, raising RETAIL_REC over two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM varied only 8.7 to 9.3 across four weeks while TRANSIT gained 10.5 points
failure_condition: When GROCERY_PHARM stays within +/-0.5 of its four-week mean and TRANSIT rises, the next-14-day mean of RETAIL_REC is not above its trailing 14-day mean.
